physicalNotes: Radius 0.13738983 Jupiter radii from Parviainen et al. 2024 (2024A&A...683A.170P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...683A.170P/abstract): 9,822.3 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0094 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Parviainen et al. 2024 (2024A&A...683A.170P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PARVIAINEN_ET_AL_2024): P 2.326318 d
sources.shape: Parviainen et al. 2024 (2024A&A...683A.170P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PARVIAINEN_ET_AL_2024): a/R* 18.43; Parviainen et al. 2024 (2024A&A...683A.170P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PARVIAINEN_ET_AL_2024): inclination 88.51 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Parviainen et al. 2024 (2024A&A...683A.170P), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname PARVIAINEN_ET_AL_2024): transit mid-time 2459255.6948195 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 5 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
